stories.title: Amazon and Google to own nearly 30% of Anthropic after IPO
stories.summary: Anthropic announced an IPO that aims to raise about $64.4 billion. Amazon will hold roughly 14.7% of the post‑IPO equity, converting promissory notes into non‑voting shares, while Google will own about 14% of the shares. Together the two cloud providers will control close to 30% of Anthropic’s outstanding stock.
stories.why: The combined stake gives the two cloud giants a significant strategic position in Anthropic’s AI platform and potential influence over its future direction.

stories.title: UK sanctions eight construction firms over West Bank settlement building
stories.summary: The United Kingdom imposed sanctions on eight construction and property‑development companies it says are involved in building Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank. The measures are the first package announced after the government said it would take a tougher approach to Israeli actions in the territory, and are intended to disrupt the firms’ financing and ability to support settlement construction.
stories.why: The sanctions aim to cut financial flows that enable settlement building in the occupied West Bank.
stories.previousTitle: UK sanctions eight firms over West Bank settlement construction
stories.previousSummary: The UK has sanctioned eight construction and property development firms it says are involved in building settlements in the occupied West Bank, the first package of measures since the government announced a tougher approach to Israeli actions in the territory. The government said the sanctions would disrupt the firms' flows of finance and their ability to support building in the West Bank. Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar called the sanctions a "hostile act targeting private, law-abiding companies".

stories.title: Canadian home sales rise 0.3% in October, still 10.6% below 2025 level
stories.summary: The Canadian Real Estate Association reported that national home sales increased 0.3 percent month‑over‑month in October 2026, but remained 10.6 percent lower than in October 2025. CREA senior economist Shaun Cathcart said activity between September and October was modest and the uptick ran opposite to analysts’ expectations. The increase came after the Bank of Canada raised its benchmark rate to 2.5 percent, its first hike since 2023.
stories.why: The data show how the housing market is responding to higher borrowing costs, informing buyers, sellers and policymakers.
stories.previousTitle: Canadian home sales edge up 0.3% in October, still 10.6% below October 2025
stories.previousSummary: National home sales rose 0.3 percent month‑over‑month in October, according to the Canadian Real Estate Association, beating some analysts’ expectations. Despite the gain, sales were 10.6 percent lower than in October 2025, reflecting a market that remains flat amid recent interest‑rate hikes and a sluggish economy.

stories.title: US probes Singapore firm Megaspeed over alleged Nvidia chip exports to China
stories.summary: The United States Department of Justice and Department of Commerce announced that they are investigating Singapore‑based computing company Megaspeed for suspected violations of U.S. export controls by facilitating the shipment of Nvidia’s high‑end AI chips to China. The probe, which began in 2024, follows concerns that such chips may have reached China despite restrictions. Authorities also allege that former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, who was involved in an extramarital affair with Nvidia founder Jensen Huang, acted as a spy for Beijing, a claim China denies.
stories.why: Trade developments can affect currencies, business costs, market access and the external balance of the economies involved.

stories.title: Ukraine damages Crimean Bridge, section collapses into water
stories.summary: Ukraine struck the Crimean Bridge with long‑range weapons in a multi‑stage operation, causing a portion of the double‑arched structure to fall into the Kerch Strait. President Volodymyr Zelensky called the attack “unprecedented,” and Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the bridge will be rebuilt. The bridge carries road and rail traffic for Russian forces to Crimea.
stories.why: The bridge is a key logistical corridor for Russian military supplies to Crimea, so its damage hampers operations and carries strong symbolic weight.
stories.previousTitle: Ukraine damages Crimean Bridge, section collapses into water
stories.previousSummary: Ukraine has severely damaged the Crimean Bridge that links Russia to occupied Crimea, with images showing a section of the structure collapsed into the water. President Volodymyr Zelensky described the strike as an unprecedented operation. In Kyiv, Mayor Vitaliy Klitschko said traffic on the Pivnichnyi and Pivdennyi bridges over the Dnipro River had partially resumed after overnight Russian attacks.

stories.title: Global Market Today: Asian shares rebound as Nvidia forecast eases AI trade concerns
stories.summary: Nvidia shares gained more than 4% in extended trading after its earnings — the first since the departure of Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang — signaled resilient demand. MSCI Inc.’s Asian equities gauge rose 0.3%, snapping a four-day run of losses, led by South Korea’s Kospi Index — a key barometer for the AI trade.

stories.title: India's current account deficit projected at 1.2% of GDP in FY27
stories.summary: A Union Bank of India report projects the current account deficit will reach about 1.2% of GDP in the 2027 fiscal year, citing high crude‑oil prices and strong gold demand as key drivers. The merchandise trade deficit widened to roughly $39.9 billion in October as imports rose sharply, while the services trade surplus stayed almost unchanged. These factors raise risks to the external balance.
stories.why: Trade developments can affect currencies, business costs, market access and the external balance of the economies involved.

stories.title: India’s retail inflation hits 6.09% in October 2026, above RBI’s 6% ceiling
stories.summary: Retail price inflation rose to 6.09% in October 2026, breaching the Reserve Bank of India’s 6% tolerance band. The increase is driven by a sharp rise in food prices, putting pressure on household budgets. The outcome has raised questions about the timing of RBI’s interest‑rate actions and the accuracy of its inflation forecasts.
stories.why: RBI action or currency-market developments can affect rupee volatility, hedging costs and foreign-exchange conditions for businesses and investors.
